full_judgment: 8. It appears that the High Court Division on consideration of the material evidence on record arrived at the findings that the document filed by the plaintiff in support of their title and possession correctly and clearly proved the title and possession in the suit land and the documents filed by the defendants were not relating to the suit land. The defendant though claimed title and possession partly by registered patta but did not file the kabuliyat and rent receipt showing that the patta was acted upon, mores, the patta do not relate to the suit land so is the case with Kabala dated 2.5.1932. On the contrary, by way of successive transfers relating back to the admitted original owner Kamini, the suit land devolved upon the plaintiff by purchase vide kabala dated 9.1.1978 (Ext. 3); the plaintiff as well proved rent receipts and led oral evidence showing their possession in the suit land. The trial Court as well found the title and possession of the suit land but the Court of appeal below without adverting to the reasoning of the trial Court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court even without reversing the finding therein.
